relevance_note: Narrative review whose Tables 1–3 and Section 2 summarize previously published individuals with TNFAIP3 variants, e.g. "Arg183Ter appeared in a 4-year-old child who presented with intermittent fever and perianal abscesses".
method_note: Paper is a narrative review (no new patients). All values come from my reading; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled rows and copied table-cell spans programmatically from the Markdown rows (checked against Tables 1-3), and every span was verified verbatim by script. LABELS: the review gives no patient labels, so each label is '<variant as printed> [<reference>]', plus the paper's relation words for relatives (e.g. 'proband's mother'). IDENTITY RULES: a table row and a Section 2 paragraph with the same variant and an overlapping reference were treated as the same entry. Where the paragraph describes one patient, row and paragraph were merged. Where the paragraph describes a family or several patients, or the row conflicts with the paragraph's proband, the row was treated as a possibly pooled family summary: its symptoms, onset and final diagnosis were not attributed to anyone, and people come from the narrative only. Rows treated this way: Trp85Glyfs*11 [33], Arg87Ter [35] ('3 weeks-43 years', family of eight; only 'one family member' is described individually), Lys91Ter [36,37], Phe224Ser fs*4 [48], Leu303fs*26 [34], Cys478Ter [54], Lys564Ter [34], His577Alafs*95 [57], Glu730Ser fs*83 [34], Gln737Ser fs*79 [62], Leu236Pro [66], Pro247Leu [68]. Kept as separate individuals because references do not match (possible duplicates): the 119 kb microdeletion case [25,27] (content resembles Table 1 row [28] but cites [25,27]); Pro268Leufs*19 table row [49] vs Turkish-family proband [73]; Thr604Argfs*93 table row [48] (age cell '28-64' may pool several people) vs 'proband patient' [49]; Section 4 'Glu187Ter' and 'Phe224Serfs*4' patients [8,44] (Glu187Ter may be a typo for Gln187Ter [44]). NOT CREATED (number of people not stated): 'Other relatives' (c.1906+2T>G), other affected relatives (Lys91Ter, Phe224Ser, Gln737Ser), the other seven Arg87Ter [35] patients, the proband's daughters (Pro268Leu [73]), the patient's children (His636fs*1), asymptomatic carriers (Ile310Thr/Gln709Arg). His577Ala's 'three children' are indistinguishable and are numbered 1-3 by me. VARIANT ATTRIBUTION: relatives get a variant row only when the text says they carry it (Glu192Lys father; Met476Ile mother) or the paragraph presents them as the patients of that variant's family (siblings, 'affected patients/members', 'Patients with this mutation', Arg87Ter 'one family member'). Other relatives have no variant row. MEFV p.Met680Ile/p.Arg761His are attributed to 'The patients' collectively, so they are left out; IL36RN c.115+6T>C is recorded for Arg183Ter [42]. CONVENTIONS: variant_type is read from the printed notation ('fs' = frameshift, 'Ter' = nonsense), from 'splice site' wording, from the Table 3 caption ('Missense mutations'), and from Table 1 (large deletion/CNV). Zygosity is 'not reported' for everyone ('heterozygous' appears only as a group statement). Inheritance is 'not reported' even where the text says 'de novo case' (exon 7-8 deletion, Pro226Leu fs*2, Leu303fs*26 [50]) because no parental testing is described. Functional results from Zhou et al. 2016 [48] and Schwarz et al. 2021 [60] are variant-level and attached to every row carrying the same variant. Table ages without units ('10', '5', '4', '29', '32') have no ISO value unless the narrative agrees with 'at the age of N'. CHECKLIST: unqualified 'fever' is not counted as recurrent fever (it needs recurrent/periodic/intermittent/episodic/episodes); a slash ('oral/genital ulcers') is not split, because the paper uses it to mean 'or'; hemolytic anemia, pancytopenia or hepatitis count as autoimmune only when the text says so. Val489Alafs*7's 'autoimmune-related ... diabetes, cytopenia, hepatitis' is mapped to type 1 diabetes, autoimmune cytopenia and autoimmune hepatitis (a judgement; Section 4 also links Val489Ala to T1D). Pericardial effusion counts as serositis; short stature or dwarfism counts as growth failure; infectious or rotavirus enteritis counts as GI inflammation. 'Initially diagnosed with interstitial lung disease' (exon 7-8 deletion) is recorded as observed with that qualifier. CONTRADICTIONS IN THE PAPER: (1) c.1906+1G>C: 'arthritis' and 'joint symptoms' vs 'There were no joint issues'; both rows emitted, checklist arthritis/arthralgia = not reported. (2) Lys564Ter vs Glu730Ser [34]: the table and the narrative swap the two families (table Lys564Ter has short stature and onset '1.5 and 21 years'; narrative Glu730Ser has 'Both of them had short stature'; table Glu730Ser has cerebral infarction, narrative Lys564Ter has cerebral thrombosis). I followed the narrative's variant-to-patient attribution. (3) Onset table vs narrative, so onset set to not reported: Arg183Ter [31] ('2 years' vs 'since his first year of age'), Leu147Glnfs*7 ('2 years' vs 'at the age of 3 months'), Cys200Ala fs*16 ('3 years' vs 'teenage years'), Gln490Ter ('19 years' vs 'since early childhood'), Asn102Ser ('29' vs 'at the age of 15'). Trp85Gly row '11 years' vs proband arthritis 'before her first year of age'; Pro247Leu row '4 years', 'De novo' vs the narrative's teenage onset and affected relatives; Leu236Pro row '13 years' vs proband '15 months'. (4) Family history: Thr129Met 'Positive' vs 'No other affected family members were found'; Val489Alafs*7 'Positive' vs 'None of his relatives presented'; Glu154Ter 'NA' vs 'family history was positive'; Asn102Ser blank vs positive. (5) Asp212Gly: table 'positive autoantibodies' vs narrative 'negative autoantibodies ... disappeared' (garbled; recorded as observed from the table). (6) Glu192Lys final diagnosis: table 'Atypical inflammatory disease' vs narrative 'PFAPA' (narrative used). (7) Section 4 cites [69] for Ala434Ter, but the table cites [30]. (8) The narrative 119 kb case says 'no additional developmental delay', whereas Table 1 row [28] lists developmental delay (kept as separate people).
